newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus seeking billions for first nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Belarus seeking billions for first nuclear plant.

text.p: Belarus, the country worst affected by radioactive fallout from the Chernobyl disaster, said on Friday it was seeking billions of dollars of investment to build its first nuclear power plant.
Energy Minister Valentin Gerasimov told a news conference that three potential sites had been chosen near the former Soviet republic's eastern border with Russia.
"These sites are acceptable from the points of view of safety and the demands of the International Atomic Energy Agency," he said.
Gerasimov said Belarus hoped to find $3.5 to $4 billion with the help of large foreign banks and companies. "Construction will begin by the end of this millenium," he added.
Energy officials have said they hoped to complete construction of the plant, which would ease Minsk's dependency on Russian oil and gas, by 2005.
Western aid to the former Soviet republic of 10 million people has totalled about $19 million amid political uncertainty sparked by a row between President Alexander Lukashenko and parliament.
The crisis eased when Lukashenko won a referendum by a landslide last month and used it to seize sweeping powers. But Western organisations accused him of acting undemocratically.

Belarus, bordering Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, has previously announced plans to build a nuclear power plant by 1988 but cancelled it after reactor number four blew up at Chernobyl near Kiev in April 1986.
About 70 per cent of the radioactive fallout blew to Belarus, where a quarter of the landscape is still contaminated and tens of thousands of people were forced to resettle.
